:::{#exm-poisson-sufficient}
#### The sum is sufficient for a Poisson rate

Let $\dsn{X} \siid \Pois(\rate)$ and $S \eqdef \sumin X_i$.
The joint mass function of the sample is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\pdf\paren{\vx ; \rate}
&= \prod_{i=1}^n \frac{e^{-\rate} \rate^{x_i}}{x_i!}
&& \text{(independent Poisson mass functions)}\\
&= e^{-n\rate} \rate^{\sumin x_i} \prod_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{x_i!}
&& \text{(collect the factors)}
\end{aligned}
$$

This has the form of @eq-factorization with
$\sfacf{t}{\rate} = e^{-n\rate} \rate^{t}$ and $\rfacf{\vx} = \prod_{i=1}^n 1 / x_i!$,
where $t = \sumin x_i$.
So the sum $S$ is [sufficient](#def-sufficient) for $\rate$ by @thm-factorization.
:::
